text:
Olen Zellweger is one of the fastest players in the league. NHL Edge has his acceleration at the very top among defensemen and his top speed at the 97th percentile, and NHL.com and Fingerlakes1 both ran pieces this week on how he uses it in Buffalo.

The trade from Anaheim gave him a bigger stage, 18:34 a night, and the start was promising. The last ten games have been quieter: one assist on 3.1 expected points, with his minutes sliding to under 13 in the loss in Florida.

Our numbers say he's been unlucky more than bad. The Sabres have scored 6.3 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, and at five on five they're better with him than without. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at the 97th percentile among defensemen for chances from the home-plate area last season, rare for a blueliner.

What to watch: the ice time. He's 23, his game is speed and offense, and he needs minutes to show it. If Buffalo's luck turns, he's a likely beneficiary.
